title: The Trench
hookLine: Salman's trench, the whole city digging on a cold morning, a rock that breaks, and Jabir's small meal that feeds the diggers (Bukhari)

lines: NO SERVANTS TO DIG FOR THEM.
cards: A cold morning, and the sound of picks on stony ground. A great army of allied tribes is coming for Medina. The biographers say the plan came from Salman the Persian: dig a trench across the open side of the city.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Anas describes the Muhajirun and the Ansar, the people of Mecca and the people of Medina, digging in the cold with no servants to do it for them.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ comes out and sees how tired and hungry they are. Today: the Trench.

teach.h: A CALL AND AN ANSWER, ACROSS A DITCH.
teach.b: What he does first is sing with them. In Anas's report, he calls out a line of verse: O Allah, the real life is the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.
The diggers call back: we are the ones who pledged to Muhammad, to strive as long as we live. A call and an answer, across a ditch.

teach.h: DUST ON HIS BELLY, FEET MADE FIRM.
teach.b: Al-Bara, also in Bukhari, adds that the Prophet carried earth himself until the dust covered his belly, reciting the verses of the poet Abdullah ibn Rawahah: without You, O Allah, we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed, so send calm down on us and make our feet firm.
Firm feet: the same gift as the night rain before Badr. Then the rock. Jabir says they hit a rock no one could break.
The Prophet took the pick and struck, and it fell apart into loose sand. An-Nasa'i's Sunan tells of three strikes, each throwing off a flash of light. Then Jabir tells something smaller and lovelier.
Seeing the Prophet's hunger, he slipped home. His wife had a little barley and a young goat; they cooked it, and Jabir quietly invited the Prophet with one or two others.
Instead the Prophet called out to the whole trench: Jabir has made a meal, come on! Jabir's wife, worried, asked if the Prophet knew how little there was. He did.
In Jabir's telling, everyone ate their fill, and the pot was still bubbling.
Many hands, one trench, one pot.

how: The Battle of the Trench, al-Khandaq, is taught in sirah classes, and the diggers' call and answer from Sahih al-Bukhari is sometimes recited as an example of the Prophet working alongside his companions.

o: a ditch the city dug together against an army
a moat built around the Ka'bah to guard it
a dry riverbed where the armies met to fight

p: the plan to dig a trench
no servants to dig for them
the verses he recited while carrying earth
a small meal that fed the trench

s: the Prophet ﷺ directed the digging but didn't dig
al-Bara says he carried earth until the dust covered his belly.
Jabir invited the whole trench to his meal
he invited the Prophet quietly, with one or two others; the Prophet called out to everyone.
in Bukhari, the hard rock fell apart into loose sand
Jabir says the Prophet took the pick and struck, and the rock became like sand.

games.q: you're Jabir. you have a little barley and one young goat, and the Prophet ﷺ is hungry. you invite him quietly, and he calls out to the whole trench. what do you do?
o: let them come, and trust him.
take the pot and hide it.
games.why: they came. in Jabir's telling, everyone ate their fill, and the pot was still bubbling.

practice: Think of a shared job ahead, at work or after a family meal, and notice where you usually stand: in front giving directions, off to the side, or not there at all.

Picture yourself in the ditch with everyone else, carrying earth, noticing who's tired and who's hungry, and what small thing you could bring, like Jabir's pot. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless the work.

wordCard.voice: The Trench: Salman's plan, dug by the people of Mecca and Medina together in the cold, with the Prophet carrying earth and singing beside them. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the trench; the battle is called the Battle of the Trench, and also of the Confederates, al-Ahzab.

carryVoice: Your line: dig together. He carried the earth too, until the dust covered him. Day seven hundred eighty-two, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2834 (Anas: the Muhajirun and Ansar digging on a cold morning with no servants; the call and answer)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4104 (al-Bara: he carried earth until dust covered his belly, reciting Ibn Rawahah's verses)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4101–4102 (Jabir: the rock turned to sand; the meal of barley and a young goat that fed the diggers)
Sunan an-Nasa'i 3176 (three strikes at a rock during the digging)
Ibn Sa'd, at-Tabaqat al-Kubra; al-Waqidi, al-Maghazi (Salman's suggestion of the trench)
